All in all, the broader picture is increasingly clear: Khamenei’s appointments do not necessarily represent the beginning of a new Iranian military doctrine. Instead, they appear to reflect the positions and ambitions of competing factions, networks of power and personalities that have been fighting for influence for years.

What may on the surface seem like a series of routine personnel changes may, in reality, be the early stage of a much larger struggle over who controls Iran’s security apparatus—and ultimately, who gets to shape the post-Ali Khamenei order.
